name: capture_item
description: Save a thought, link, follow-up, idea, or anything the user dumps. Use this BY DEFAULT whenever the user shares something that isn't a direct question or instruction. Never make the user decide where to put a thought - just capture it. The assistant can re-categorize captured items later.

content.description: The raw content to capture. Preserve the user's wording when possible.

category.description: Best-guess category. Default to 'thought' if unclear.

project_name.description: Project this relates to, if obvious. Omit if unclear.

name: surface_next_action
description: Return the next concrete action on a project, specified at the level of 'open this file, your cursor here, type these three words.' Use when the user asks what to work on, or when they're stuck. If the user says the action is still too big, call again with a smaller_than parameter to shrink it further.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to highest-priority active project (likely Simmer) if omitted.

smaller_than.description: Optional: if a previous suggestion was too big, describe what was suggested so this call returns something smaller.

name: log_blocker
description: Record that the user is stuck on something specific. Critical for stall detection - blockers are how Spotter knows the user is avoiding something vs. just busy.

reason.description: Why it's blocked, in the user's words if available.

project_name.description: Which project this blocker is on.

task_id.description: Optional: task ID this blocker is attached to.

name: query_memory
description: Search captured items, tasks, blockers, or workspace facts. Use this when the user references something past ('what was that thing about X', 'did I mention Y', 'where did we leave off on Z').

query.description: Search keywords. FTS5 is used under the hood - keep queries focused on content words.

scope.description: Which memory layer to search. Use 'all' if uncertain.

name: update_workspace_doc
description: Write to the Google Doc workspace. The doc has six sections: Today, Captured This Week, Active Tasks, Blockers, Done This Week, Long-term Context. Use this when something needs to be persistent and human-readable, separate from the database.

section.description: Which section of the doc to update.

action.description: Append a new line/bullet to the section, or replace the whole section.

content.description: The text to write. Plain text, one item per line.

name: draft_message
description: Generate a draft email, Slack message, or text message for the user to review and send. Use this whenever the user mentions needing to reply, send, or message someone. ALWAYS draft - don't just remind. Present the draft and ask for approval.

recipient.description: Who the message is to. Name or relationship if known.

purpose.description: What the user wants to communicate.

tone.description: Tone preference. Default: direct and brief, matching the user's voice.

background.description: Any context the message needs to reference.

name: schedule_intent
description: Capture a scheduling intent - something the user wants to schedule, deadline they're committing to, or event they want to remember. V1 does NOT touch Google Calendar - this just records the intent. The user will see captured intents in the morning brief.

description.description: What's being scheduled. E.g. 'lunch with Sam', 'Simmer launch'.

when_text.description: When, in the user's words. E.g. 'next Tuesday afternoon', 'before end of month'.

name: name_the_stall
description: Call this when the user appears to be stalling on a project - especially Simmer. Signs: keeps capturing new ideas instead of doing the next step, has been avoiding the same concrete task for multiple days, brings up cosmetic concerns when launch is the actual blocker, or tries to start a new project while an existing one is at 70-80% completion. Be direct in your response. Do not soften.

project_name.description: Which project the user is stalling on.

avoided_step.description: What specific step they're avoiding. Be concrete.

pattern_observed.description: What behavior tipped you off. E.g. 'asking about Chef Mode design while landing page is unfinished'.

name: update_task_status
description: Update the status of an existing task or project when the user says something is finished, paused, waiting on someone/something, dropped, or should be reopened. Resolve the target from recent context: pass the numeric id when you have one (tool results show 'task #N'), otherwise pass the name — case-insensitive partial match is fine. If the result says multiple tasks match, retry with the exact id.

target_type.description: Whether to update a single task or a whole project.

id.description: Exact task or project id, if known from recent context. Preferred over name.

name.description: Task title or project name to match. Required when id is omitted.

status.description: New status. Tasks: open | in_progress | done | paused | waiting | dropped. Projects: active | paused | done.

name: schedule_reminder
description: Create a scheduled message the user will receive later: a one-shot reminder or a recurring check-in. Resolve natural-language times ('at 3pm', 'tomorrow morning', 'every evening at 6') into a concrete LOCAL date and time using the Current time block in your context, and pass it as when_local. For recurring requests ('every evening at 6') set recurrence and pass the next upcoming occurrence as when_local. kind=reminder sends the message verbatim; kind=checkin has Spotter write the message at fire time from your instruction. Do not use this for the user's vague future intents with no set time — that's schedule_intent.

when_local.description: Resolved local date and time, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (24-hour), in the user's timezone shown in the Current time block.

kind.description: reminder = send the message text verbatim. checkin = generate a message at fire time from the instruction in message.

message.description: For reminder: the exact text to send. For checkin: the instruction for what the check-in should cover.

recurrence.description: Set for recurring triggers; omit for one-shot.

name: set_project_goal
description: Set or update a project's goal - the target state in plain language, e.g. 'Simmer is live with real users signing up and paying'. Use when the user states what a project is for, where it should end up, or what success looks like. Optionally record the current bottleneck at the same time. If the result says no milestones exist, offer to decompose the goal.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to the highest-priority active project if omitted.

goal.description: The target state in plain language. Preserve the user's wording where possible.

current_bottleneck.description: Optional: the single thing most blocking progress right now, if the user stated it.

name: decompose_goal
description: Break a project's goal into ordered milestones. TWO-STEP tool. Step 1: call with just project_name - the result is the project's goal, bottleneck, open tasks, recent activity, and existing milestones. Step 2: think about what actually stands between that current state and the goal (do NOT just restate the goal), then call again with the milestones array to write them. First milestone = the one to work toward right now. Writing replaces unfinished milestones; done ones are kept.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to the highest-priority active project if omitted.

title.description: Concrete, verifiable state - a step, not the whole goal.

description.description: Optional detail: what done looks like, key sub-steps.

milestones.description: Ordered milestones to write, first = work toward now. OMIT on the first call - provide only after reading the context the first call returns.

name: update_milestone
description: Update a milestone's status when one is completed, being started, or dropped. Pass the numeric id when known (tool results show 'milestone #N'), otherwise the title - case-insensitive partial match is fine. Marking one active demotes any other active milestone in that project (only one active at a time); completing or dropping the active one auto-activates the next pending milestone.

id.description: Exact milestone id, if known from recent context. Preferred over title.

title.description: Milestone title to match. Required when id is omitted.

name: set_bottleneck
description: Record the single thing most blocking a project right now. Use when the user identifies what's actually in the way ('the whole thing is stuck on X'). Different from log_blocker: log_blocker records one specific stuck item; the bottleneck is project-level strategic state used by briefs and next-action reasoning.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to the highest-priority active project if omitted.

bottleneck.description: The single most-blocking thing, in plain language.

name: prepare_handoff
description: Generate a ready-to-paste prompt that hands ONE task or milestone to Claude Code for execution. Spotter holds strategy; Claude Code executes. Call the tool to get the assembled context (objective, goal, bottleneck, related work, blockers, workspace facts), then compose the prompt it describes - Objective / Context / Constraints / Definition of done - and output it inside ONE fenced code block. Use when the user asks for a handoff, a prompt for Claude Code, or 'give me the prompt to go build this'. With no target specified, defaults to the project's active milestone (else its next task).

target_type.description: What kind of thing is being handed off. Required when passing an id; optional with a title.

id.description: Exact task or milestone id, if known from recent context.

title.description: Task or milestone title to match when no id is known. Case-insensitive partial match.

project_name.description: Project to default from when no target is given. Defaults to the highest-priority active project.

name: list_job_applications
description: List the user's tracked job applications - company, role, status, date applied, source, notes - with a pipeline summary. Use whenever the user asks about their job search, applications, pipeline, or a specific company they applied to. Applications are added and updated on the web dashboard; this tool is read-only.

status.description: Optional: only applications in this status. Omit for all.

name: query_events
description: Search the event log - what ACTUALLY happened: commits, PR merges, Claude Code session notes, captures - ranked by recency and source confidence (a fresh commit outranks an old remembered claim; superseded entries are excluded). Use for 'what happened on X', 'where does Y stand', 'did anything ship', 'what did I work on recently'. Prefer this over query_memory for questions about recent state or activity, and cite the age and source of what you report.

query.description: Optional keywords; all must appear in an event. Omit to list recent activity.

project_name.description: Optional: limit to one project's events.

days.description: Look-back window in days. Default 30, max 365.

name: start_session
description: The user is STARTING a work session ('starting on Simmer', 'about to work on X', 'sitting down to code'). Call this to pull the warm-start context: where the last session left off, what has moved since (commits, notes), the active milestone, the next action on record, and open blockers. Then give them a short warm start pointing at the ONE thing to do first.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to the highest-priority active project.

name: end_session
description: The user is ENDING a work session ('done for now', 'wrapping up', 'calling it'). Capture where they left off so the next session starts warm: summarize what they said happened into note (and next if stated), or ask one short question to get it if they gave nothing. Writes a session_note event into memory.

project_name.description: Which project. Defaults to the highest-priority active project.

note.description: Where things stand: what was worked on / what happened, 1-3 sentences.

next.description: Optional: the stated next step for next session.

name: supersede_event
description: Retire a stale event when newer information contradicts it. Use when query_events surfaces something you can SEE is outdated (an old claim contradicted by a newer commit, session note, or what the user just said). Pass the newer event as replacement_event_id when one exists; otherwise the stated reason becomes a correction event. The retired event stops surfacing in retrieval. Never retire something merely old - only something contradicted.

event_id.description: The stale event to retire (query_events results show 'event #N').

reason.description: What newer information contradicts it, specifically.

replacement_event_id.description: Optional: the newer event that supersedes it, if one exists in the log.
